minutes_text:
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  December 13, 2016

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Ury at 5:01 p.m., on December 13, 2016, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on December 8, 2016, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Raths (arrived at 5:32 p.m.)
  Council Member Sachs
  Council Member Schlicht (arrived at 5:55 p.m.)
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ury

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Dennis Wilberg, City Manager
  William P. Curley III, City Attorney
  Keith Rattay, Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services
  Cheryl Dyas, Director of Administrative Services
  Karen Hamman, City Clerk

RECESS

At the hour of 5:01 p.m., Mayor Ury declared a recess. The City Council reconvened at 6:02 p.m.
with all five City Council Members present.

INVOCATION: Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Raths

City Council Minutes  1  December 13, 2016
 PRESENTATIONS

P1.  Mayor’s State of the City Address

  Mayor Ury presented the State of the City video address.

P2.  Presentation to and Comments from Outgoing Council Member Cathy Schlicht

  Mayor Ury, Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum and various dignitaries presented Council Member
  Schlicht with certificates and plaques in recognition of her service. Council Member
  Schlicht made outgoing comments as well.

P3.  Presentation to and Comments from Outgoing Mayor/Council Member Frank Ury

  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum and various dignitaries presented Mayor Ury with certificates
  and plaques in recognition of his service. Mayor Ury also made outgoing comments.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Raths, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Raths, Sachs, Schlicht, and Ury
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

1.  Waive Reading of Ordinances and Resolutions

  Approved the reading by title of all ordinances and resolutions and declared that said titles
  which appear on the public agenda shall be determined to have been read by title and further
  reading waived.

2.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the minutes for the Regular Meeting of November 22, 2017, as presented.

3.  Official Results of the November 8, 2016, General Municipal Election

  Adopted Resolution 16-57 Reciting the Fact of the General Municipal Election Held On
  November 8, 2016, Declaring the Result and Such Other Matters as Provided by Law.

4.  Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended

City Council Minutes  2  December 13, 2016
   Received reports.

5.  Check Register Dated November 16, 2016 in the Amount of $1,203,213.53

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Check Register Dated November 18, 2016 in the Amount of $626,028.76

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

7.  Check Register Dated November 25, 2016 in the Amount of $1,255,124.27

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

8.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2016

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing  Authority  (MVCDFA)
  Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October 2016

  Received and filed.

10.  Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for October
  2016

  Received and filed.

11.  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly
  Report for October 2016

  Received and filed.

ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Sharon Cody, M.V.: thanked Frank Ury for his wonderful support of her, the animal shelter and
the shelter volunteers.

Jerry Bryant, M.V.: stated that he is in favor of Greg Raths serving as Mayor in 2017.

Jim Leach, SMWD, M.V.: announced that Santa Margarita Water District is in the process of
implementing the third phase of a five-year rate structure adjustment and that notice of the change
in rates has been mailed to residents.
City Council Minutes  3  December 13, 2016
 Dan Avery, M.V.: thanked Frank Ury for the positive leadership that he has provided while on the
City Council and, on behalf of his dog Hunter, he thanked Mr. Ury for the dog park.

RECESS

At the hour of 7:14 p.m., Mayor Ury recessed the meeting. The City Council reconvened at 7:36
p.m. with Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, Council Member Raths and Council Member Sachs in
attendance.

CITY COUNCIL ORGANIZATION

12.  Administration of Oaths of Office

  Jack Kelley administered the ceremonial Oath of Office to his wife, Trish Kelley and Vicki
  Goodell presented the ceremonial Oath of Office to her husband, Brian Goodell. City Clerk
  Karen Hamman presented Certificates of Election to Council Members Kelley and
  Goodell.

PUBLIC COMMENTS (Continued)

Cameron Knauerhaze, M.V.: stated that he is proud to live in Mission Viejo and he announced that
he is an applicant for the Community Services Commission and he hopes to serve the City that he
loves.

Jay Djavid, M.V.: expressed his support for Greg Raths for Mayor.

The following did not address the Council but indicated on their “Request to Speak” form that they
support Greg Raths for Mayor: Siavash Zadeh, M.V. and Stu Evans, M.V.

The following expressed support for Wendy Bucknum for Mayor: Karen Bargubus, M.V.; Teri
Perea, M.V.; and Skye Anderson, M.V.

Art Villalovos, M.V.: on behalf of the Heritage Committee, he presented Mission Viejo History
books to Council Members Goodell and Kelley.

CITY COUNCIL ORGANIZATION (Continued)

13.  Election of Mayor and Mayor Pro Tem for 2017

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to appoint
  Wendy Bucknum as Mayor for the remainder of the year and for 2017.

  Council Member Raths discussed his involvement in the community and outside
  organizations and expressed his interest in serving as Mayor or Mayor Pro Tem.

City Council Minutes  4  December 13, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

  Motion made by Mayor Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to appoint Ed
  Sachs as Mayor Pro Tem for the remainder of the meeting and for 2017.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

CONSENT CALENDAR (CONTINUED)

Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve the
Consent Calendar as outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

14.  First Amendment to Contract Agreement with City’s Independent Auditing Firm,
  Davis Farr LLP

  Approved First Amendment with Davis Farr LLP, to include Agreed Upon Procedures set
  forth in Exhibit 1 and increasing the contract by $11,000.00, for a total contract amount
  not to exceed $84,220.00.

15.  Annual Measure M-2 Expenditure Report for Fiscal Year Ended June 30, 2016

  Adopted Resolution 16-58 Adopting the Measure M2 Expenditure Report for the City of
  Mission Viejo

16.  Master Agreement for Federal Aid Projects and Program Supplement Agreement for
  Trabuco Road and Marguerite Parkway Pavement Rehabilitation (CIP 837)

  Adopted Resolution 16-59 Approving and Authorizing Execution of Administering
  Agency-State Agreement No. 12-5451F15 and Program Supplement No. 025-F for
  Federal-Aid Projects Between the State Department of Transportation and the City of
  Mission Viejo.
City Council Minutes  5  December 13, 2016
 ITEMS REMOVED FROM THE CONSENT CALENDAR

PUBLIC HEARINGS

17.  Ordinances Adopting the 2016 California Building and Fire Codes (2nd Reading)

  Director of Community Development Elaine Lister and Building Manager Jay Elbettar
  presented the staff report and answered the City Council Members questions.

  At the hour of 8:11 p.m., Mayor Bucknum opened the public hearing. After hearing no
  requests to speak, Mayor Bucknum closed the public hearing.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to (1)
  adopt Ordinance 16-319 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of Mission
  Viejo Adopting by Reference the 2016 Editions of the California Building, Residential,
  Plumbing, Electrical, Mechanical, Green Building Standards, Historical Building, and
  Existing Building Codes, and the 2015 Editions of the International Swimming Pool and
  Spa Code and International Property Maintenance Code, together, with certain Appendices
  and Amendments Thereto, and Amending Title 8 of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code;”
  (2) adopt Resolution 16-60 Setting Forth Findings for Required Amendments to the 2016
  California Building Code Relative to Local Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic
  Conditions; (3) adopt Ordinance 16-320 entitled “An Ordinance of the City Council of
  the City of Mission Viejo Adopting by Reference the 2016 California Fire Code, Together
  with Certain Amendments and Deletions”; and (4) adopt Resolution 16-61 Setting Forth
  Findings for Required Amendments to the 2016 California Fire Code Relative to Local
  Climatic, Topographic, and Geologic Conditions.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

18.  An Extension, for a Maximum Period of 10 Months and 15 Days, to Urgency
  Ordinance No. 16-321, an Interim Zoning Ordinance Adopted as an Urgency
  Measure Pursuant to Government Code Section 65858, and Establishing a
  Temporary Moratorium on the Approval of Permits for New or Expanded Uses
  Involving, Directly or Indirectly, the Collective Transport of Groups of People and
  Associated Group Assembly in the City.

  City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.

  At the hour of 8:20 p.m., Mayor Bucknum opened the public hearing.

City Council Minutes  6  December 13, 2016
   Craig Foster, M.V.: speaking on behalf of 449 Group, he expressed opposition to the
  extension of the ordinance and the temporary moratorium.

  Mayor Bucknum closed the public hearing at 8:31 p.m.

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs asked the Mayor to consider appointing two Council Members to
  an ad hoc committee for the purpose of studying this matter and providing
  recommendations to the Council.

  Motion made by Council Member Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve an extension, for a maximum period of 10 months and 15 days, to Urgency
  Ordinance No. 16-321 (Ordinance 16-321A) an Interim Zoning Ordinance adopted as an
  urgency measure pursuant to Government Code Section 65858, and establishing a
  temporary moratorium on the approval of permits for new or expanded uses involving,
  directly or indirectly, the collective transport of groups of people and associated group
  assembly in the City; and (2) direct staff to further study and explore appropriate regulatory
  options and return with a recommendation to City Council regarding the structuring of
  zoning over a new use/facility and the expansion of an existing use/ facility involving
  directly or indirectly, the collective transport of groups of people and associated group
  assembly.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Sachs
  NOES:  Raths
  ABSENT:  None

NEW BUSINESS

19.  Ordinance Amending Various Sections of Title 10 of the Mission Viejo Municipal
  Codes

  Assistant City Manager/Director of Public Services Keith Rattay presented the staff report.

  Gail De Young, Animal Services Manager, answered the City Council Member's questions.

  Council Member Kelley requested that on page 4 of the Ordinance, under Vicious Dog,
  item number 2, the word "substantial" be changed to "severe” for consistency with item
  number 1 above.

  Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to
  introduce Ordinance 17-322, as amended, Adopting Comprehensive Revisions to Title 10
  of the Mission Viejo Municipal Code as Set Forth on Attachment B. Amendment: change
  the word "substantial" to "severe” on page 4, item 2 under Vicious Dog.

City Council Minutes  7  December 13, 2016
   On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

20.  Foothill/Eastern & San Joaquin Hills Transportation Corridor Agencies Report

  Mayor Pro Tem Sachs presented the report.

STAFF REPORTS

Lt. Ken Binning provided holiday public safety reminders regarding package and auto thefts. He
also encouraged residents to consider the Neighborhood Watch Program which is a way for
homeowners to work together and with law enforcement to reduce or eliminate crime from their
neighborhoods.

21.  Pre-Budget Discussion Meeting Date

  The Council discussed potential dates for a pre-budget meeting in January or early
  February however, no date was set.

City Manager Wilberg drew the Council Members’ attention to a packet of information that was
distributed regarding a connectivity plan for the lake loop and Oso Creek Trail.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley thanked the Mission Viejo Activities Committee for hosting and
sponsoring Santa's Arrival. She attended with her grandsons who had a fantastic time and enjoyed
seeing Santa arrive on a fire truck. She reminded residents that they can visit Santa Claus in his
workshop at the Civic Center every Wednesday, Saturday and Sunday from 6:00 to 8:00 p.m. and
visits are free. Again, she noted, that the Mission Viejo Activities Committee has worked very
hard this season and she thanked the volunteers. Council Member Kelley announced that the
Marine Adoption Committee is conducting a toy drive for the City’s adopted Marines of
Headquarters Battalion 1st Division at Camp Pendleton. Boxes have been placed at city hall and
at various locations throughout the city and she asked residents to please consider supporting the
Marines by donating a toy. Council Member Kelley thanked the voters for electing her and shared
that she was humbled and honored by the election results. She thanked outgoing Council Members
Ury and Schlicht for their service and she thanked Council Member Raths for his support during
the campaign. Finally, Council Member Kelley thanked her campaign partner, Council Member

City Council Minutes  8  December 13, 2016
 Brian Goodell. In closing she wished her colleagues and residents a Merry Christmas, Happy
Hanukkah and happy holidays.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell announced that he recently volunteered to offer testimony to the Public
Utilities Commission (PUC) at a South Orange County Economic Coalition Committee meeting
with respect to the redevelopment of a substation in San Juan Capistrano that will bring redundancy
and protection for all of south Orange County. Council Member Goodell noted that in the event of
a catastrophic loss of the substation in San Clemente, there will be a power loss that puts a lot of
people at risk. He said that he will soon and again be offering testimony in San Francisco to the
California PUC to make sure that Mission Viejo voices are heard for a very necessary and long
overdue project that will preserve the health and safety of the people of Mission Viejo all of south
Orange County. Council Member Goodell thanked everyone who supported him in the election
and he thanked Council Member Kelley for helping him with his campaign. He said that he is
excited to serve the City in the capacity of Council Member and he looks forward to exciting times
ahead.

Council Member Raths

Council Member Raths congratulated and thanked former Council Member Ury for his 12 years
of service and said that he learned a lot from Frank Ury. He also thanked Cathy Schlicht for her 8
years of service. Council Member Raths congratulated Brian Goodell and Trish Kelley on the
election and he welcomed them to the City Council. He further congratulated Wendy Bucknum
on being selected Mayor and Ed Sachs for his selection as Mayor Pro Tem. He said that the current
Council is a great team and will lead the City through another amazing year in 2017 and he looks
forward to continuing to serve with his colleagues. Council Member Raths stated that he
understands why senior military officers don't get into politics because it can be hard and slow to
get things done. However, he said that General James Mattis as Defense Secretary and General
John Kelly who will run Homeland Security will be great and he looks forward to their leadership
along with the new President, Donald Trump. In closing, Council Member Raths reminded
residents of the Chamber of Commerce casino night mixer on Wednesday, December 14 from 5:30
to 8:30 p.m. at the Murray Community Center.

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs

Mayor Pro Tem Sachs stated that while serving on the Orange County Fire Authority (OCFA)
Board of Directors he learned that there has been a recent uptick of fires in the City of Mission
Viejo. Residents and homeowners need to take particular care during the holidays to understand
the dangers of lighting while trees are drying out. He asked residents to please make it a holiday
that everyone is happy to remember. He also shared the sad news of the death of OCFA Fire
Captain Eric Weuve who took his life earlier today when he jumped to the freeway from the Crown
Valley bridge in Mission Viejo. Mayor Pro Tem Sachs said that the community’s heart goes out
to his family and also to the family of the driver of the vehicle that struck Captain Weuve.

City Council Minutes  9  December 13, 2016
 Mayor Bucknum

Mayor Bucknum stated that she is honored to serve the City in the leadership capacity of
Mayor. She said she cares very much about Mission Viejo and she has been involved in the
community for a long time. She also said that she looks forward to learning about the many groups
of people and interests in the City and she is excited to be able to work with the current team of
Council Members who are servant leaders with the primary goal of serving the residents. Mayor
Bucknum discussed her goals for the year including more public engagement via public meetings
and more TV programs, communication on the web, social media and printed publications for
heightened citizen engagement. She said that the Council wants to continue to enhance Mission
Viejo’s economy and the Economic Development Committee has done a phenomenal job. Mayor
Bucknum shared said that she would like to see the City take bold steps in business enhancement
to retain businesses in this competitive market. She thanked all of the candidates who ran for
election and specifically Council Members Kelley and Goodell. She also thanked Frank Ury for
his mentorship, vision and innovation and said that his time on the Council will benefit Mission
Viejo well into the future. Mayor Bucknum further thanked Congresswoman Mimi Walters,
Senator Bates, Assemblyman Brough and Supervisory Bartlett for their representation at tonight’s
meeting and their unwavering support when Mission Viejo needs them. She thanked the families
and friends who support the Council Members as they serve the City and wished everyone a Merry
Christmas, Happy Hanukkah and happy New Year. In closing, Mayor Bucknum noted that she
will be adjourning the meeting in memory of longtime Mission Viejo volunteer, Jerry Silverstein.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 9:12 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this
session, Mayor Bucknum adjourned the meeting in memory of Jerry Silverstein, to Tuesday,
January 10, 2017, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________________
Karen Hamman, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of January 10, 2017

City Council Minutes  10  December 13, 2016
